t: An Ionian island state off Asia Minor, settled c. 1000 BCE, that became one of the richest cities in the Greek world.
Its wine, mastic and fleet made it a leading member of the Ionian League and, later, an autonomous naval ally of Athens.
Chios had early popular institutions and, by ancient accounts, more slaves than any Greek state except Sparta.
dyk: Herodotus credits Glaucus of Chios with inventing the welding of iron; he made a famous iron stand for a silver bowl dedicated at Delphi by Alyattes of Lydia.
ev: Ionian Greeks settle Chios, which joins the Ionian League
An inscribed law refers to a popular council on Chios
Chios sends 100 ships to the Battle of Lade
Chios revolts from Athens with Spartan support
Chios becomes a founding member of the Second Athenian League
Athenian general Chabrias is killed attacking the harbour of Chios in the Social War
Mithridates VI of Pontus deports the Chians towards the Black Sea

f.predecessor: Pre-Greek and Bronze Age settlements of Chios
f.successor: Roman Republic (free city in the province of Asia)
